insights.summary: FY26 revenue rose 89% to ₹301 Cr and net profit 79% to ₹46 Cr, with EBITDA margin of 22.6%; H2 FY26 revenue was ₹179 Cr. Aimtron bought a US electronics maker (ICS, renamed AIC, Decatur, Illinois) at about 11% EBITDA margin, and the group order book is about ₹600 Cr. For FY27 management gave ₹450-550 Cr revenue, 20-22% EBITDA and about 15% PAT margin, but operating cash flow was negative about ₹40 Cr as inventory and receivables grew.

what_changed.text: Acquired ICS in Illinois (now AIC), adding about $17 million of FY27 revenue at lower margins
FY27 revenue range ₹450-550 Cr, 20-22% EBITDA margin
First greenfield SMT line now by end FY27 or Q1 FY28 (was Q3 or early Q4); mechanical setup first
$12 million data-centre UPS design order from a Fortune 500 company
Further acquisitions put on hold given the geopolitical situation

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: I think we are very conservative and we are very transparent in numbers and commitment.

analyst_questions.answer: FY27 range of ₹450-550 Cr includes AIC; the chairman admitted the maths doesn't fit and called the range conservative.
Fast growth and ODM work need inventory; cash flow expected to stabilise only near ₹1,000 Cr revenue.
Costs cut using Indian back-office staff; EBITDA expected from about 11% to 18-20% within a year or two.
The market is big; Aimtron targets niche, complex, rugged electronics.

red_flags.text: Operating cash flow about –₹40 Cr in FY26; about ₹240 Cr tied up in inventory and receivables.
Guidance doesn't reconcile: AIC alone is about ₹170 Cr of the ₹150-250 Cr expected increase.
Gross margin fell from about 31% in H1 to 28% in H2 FY26.
The lower-margin acquisition will weigh on consolidated margins until it improves.

watch_next: H1 FY27 revenue towards the ₹450-550 Cr full-year range
Greenfield mechanical setup by Q4 FY27

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Electronics system design and manufacturing: PCB assembly, box build (65-70% of revenue), ODM design; rugged and agritech electronics through the US subsidiary
business_snapshot.customers: Global OEMs (including a Fortune 500 data-centre firm), telecom, power, industrial, drone and defence PSU customers
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: About 70% domestic and 30% international; India and US the top two markets
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: China-plus-one, data centres (UPS), Wi-Fi 6/7 telecom gear, railways and defence electronics
